A Cut release can validate its version candidate, then merge after master has advanced. The existing metadata guard correctly stops publication, but the failed journal blocks later cuts and the retry advice cannot repair the immutable source.

Recheck the base immediately before requesting the normal merge, retain exact post-merge validation, and automatically retire proven unpublished terminal candidates. Retirement preserves the draft and assets, records a durable tombstone, verifies readback, and lets the next fresh run finish interrupted cleanup. Merged versions remain intact. Review/queue waits, active runs, provider intents, partial publications and uncertain outcomes stay protected.

Closes #41.

## Test plan

- **Base moves during validation or at merge:** synthetic candidate tests reject the first case before requesting a merge and retain exact-tree rejection for the late race.
- **Cleanup succeeds or loses its response:** the same journal/assets are retained under an abandoned identity; the original run cannot restart. Fresh cuts unblock only after verified cleanup. Interrupted and cancelled preparation is reconciled by the next run.
- **Publication may have started:** all operation states, unknown assets, active runs and possible provider-job execution remain blocking. Owned open version PRs require exact identity checks before closure.

Final-head [CI passed](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37815013722): **314 unit tests**, including the real Git merge regression, **25 PostgreSQL/Auth integration tests**, **five account-browser scenarios**, all typechecks and server/web builds. Locally, 40 focused tests passed; captured child-process pipes blocked ten other tests, which passed in Linux CI.

This is non-UI workflow behavior. [Raw results, reproduction, exact source/base, complete scope and retained failure evidence](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/blob/172cd5b96b020b8c82fe14f09b29ec253d0d5b53/final-report.md).

## Limits and recovery

[Cut release run 37716705314](https://github.com/MChartier/little-say/actions/runs/37716705314/job/113114712659) validated a version candidate, but master advanced before its version PR merged. The generic retry advice cannot repair this stale immutable plan, and its unresolved draft journal blocks subsequent cuts.

This follows the user's request to investigate and fix the failed action, plus the requirement that failed unpublished releases clean up automatically. It is a focused follow-up to #27; preserve that issue's original scope and owner history.

## Requirements and acceptance

- Recheck the pinned source/default base before requesting the normal version-PR merge. Diagnose base movement clearly; preserve exact metadata/tree, candidate/base-CI and branch-protection safeguards, including rejection of a race after the last check.
- Automatically retire terminal failed unpublished candidates under a nonblocking abandoned identity, retaining original journals/assets, source identities and the reason. Preserve already merged version metadata.
- Use durable abandonment/tombstone lookup before planning or journal creation so an abandoned run ID cannot be recreated. Historical workflow checkouts lack this safeguard and must not be rerun after abandonment.
- Recover from runner interruption/cancellation through serialized reconciliation on a subsequent fresh run, as well as failure cleanup where supported. Verify retirement readback; an incomplete, ambiguous or failed cleanup must retain blocking state.
- Preserve recoverable review/approval/merge-queue and retry states. Retain partial publications and uncertain provider intents/outcomes for reconciliation; absence of a success receipt alone must never establish that nothing was published.
- Retire an open version PR only after verifying its ownership, exact candidate/base and retirement scope. Never revert merged versions, delete recovery evidence, or disturb another active run/branch.
- Cover the observed base-movement failure, late merge races, idempotent cleanup, lost cleanup responses, interruption/cancellation, abandoned-ID retries, concurrency, review/queue waits, and partial/uncertain publication with maintained synthetic regressions and safe dry runs. Provide concise non-UI CLI/JSON evidence and applicable checks in one focused draft PR.

## Implementation plan

1. Reproduce the source/candidate/merged-tree mismatch with local Git fixtures and injected GitHub/provider responses; distinguish terminal stale-source failure from retryable and uncertain states.
2. Add pre-merge base validation and structured failure diagnosis without relaxing post-merge validation.
3. Add serialized, idempotent retirement/reconciliation with durable run tombstones, verified retained-asset identity and fail-closed readback. Reuse the workflow's release concurrency boundary.
4. Update recovery instructions and run focused regressions plus applicable repository checks. Keep generated evidence on retained nonmerged records, outside product history.

Implementation and testing must not rerun a real release, mutate the existing live candidate, merge, publish, invoke provider operations, spend on EAS builds, submit to stores, deploy, retrieve secrets or configure credentials. Any proposed recovery of the historical run must be described separately, not executed.
